markdown_report:
At 10% progress, prioritize **history-relative temporal bias within corrected HSTU**, conditional on verified timestamp alignment at training and prediction. Its benefit remains a hypothesis requiring host validation; uniform-only multi-negative training remains the essential feasible control.

**Insights and directions.** Three starting-point insights guide the proposal. (1) Users report stale interests crowding out current needs. Historical spacing may identify changes within history, but cannot identify inactivity after the latest event without an observed request time. (2) Broad associations outrank direct task connections. Temporal context could distinguish sustained activity from isolated historical interest, but cannot establish equipment compatibility or replacement demand. (3) Industrial has the highest measured training misranking rate, 5.05%, and tenth-percentile margin 0.8873. This identifies weak separation without establishing its cause; Electronics/CDs’ large margins remain score-scale dependent, and embedding cosines do not establish collapse.

Three literature insights constrain implementation. (1) [HSTU](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.17152v3) adds positional/temporal bias before SiLU; its reference implementation uses shifted query timestamps, requiring an explicit leakage-free adaptation here. (2) [LIC](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.15817) motivates useful older behavior, while the [recency study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.09722) cautions against unconditional decay. (3) [Sampling research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) finds dataset-dependent tradeoffs, so strong training margins do not justify automatically escalating negative difficulty.

**Framework.** Organize research along three directions: context selection, candidate discrimination, and representation grounding.

| Direction | Existing approach | Proposed experiment | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Context | Position-only HSTU | Learned position-plus-history-time bias | Timestamp interface unverified; request-time inactivity unobserved |
| Discrimination | Uniform negatives | Uniform multi-negative control, then moderate lexical curriculum | Unknown false negatives |
| Grounding | Item IDs | Joint title/description encoding | Compatibility remains unverified |

**Candidate assessment.** Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder. Each cell gives a positive and a limitation.

| Idea | Scores | Critical assessment by axis |
|---|---|---|
| Temporal HSTU | 3/6/6/5/7 | O: targeted adaptation, established mechanism; P: reusable spacing signal, interface conditional; U: targets stale within-history associations and weak current-task connections, cannot detect post-history inactivity; M: tests Industrial separation, temporal cause unmeasured; D: compact table, substantial alignment/export work |
| Moderate lexical negatives | 5/6/7/7/4 | O: curriculum combination, familiar sampling; P: sharper discrimination, false negatives; U: challenges broad similarity, may penalize valid alternatives; M: targets separation, training gains may not generalize; D: inference unchanged, filtering requires care |
| Joint text–ID encoding | 4/7/7/5/7 | O: constrained adaptation, existing precedent; P: sparse-item sharing, noisy text; U: exposes specific attributes, cannot certify compatibility; M: may improve representations, no collapse established; D: one network, larger implementation |

**Selected algorithm.** Add zero-initialized, head-specific temporal tables using only observed historical pair gaps. This explicitly targets two reported failures: old interests within history crowding out stronger recent connections, and broad historical associations displacing sustained task-level patterns. Both links are hypotheses; temporal information cannot establish unsupported equipment needs. Industrial’s measured separation weakness supplies the model-facing target.

Keep causal masking, positional bias, gating, normalization and baseline loss. Apply finite bias before SiLU and valid-token/causal masking afterward. Unlike the shifted official implementation, query row i uses t_i, never the prediction target’s timestamp. Retain nonmonotonic learned weights.

First verify aligned timestamps through sampling, ModelView and exported prediction; otherwise defer temporal training without fabricating times. Predeclare affordable matched comparisons, checkpoint opportunities and stopping rules. Diagnose timestamp-origin invariance and shuffled-gap sensitivity in-sample. Select solely by pinned sampled macro validation HR@10, reporting all four category scores. Preserve four routed checkpoints, predictor consistency, diagnostic interfaces, seeds and training limits. Repeated selection can overfit validation, and sampled HR does not establish full-catalog ranking quality ([selection bias](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html); [sampled metrics](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)).

idea.description: Conditionally extend corrected HSTU with jointly learned history-relative temporal attention bias, retaining one independently trained network and one selected checkpoint per category. Implement the temporal extension only after verifying aligned historical timestamps at both training and prediction; otherwise retain the corrected position-only HSTU and prioritize its uniform multi-negative control.
idea.motivation: User feedback identifies old interests within history and broad historical associations displacing direct recent connections. Historical spacing may distinguish sustained activity from isolated past interest, addressing these two user-facing failures as explicit hypotheses. Industrial’s 5.05% training negative-beats-positive rate and 0.8873 tenth-percentile margin identify a measured model-facing separation weakness, although neither establishes a temporal cause. Pairwise historical gaps cannot identify inactivity after the last interaction: identical histories yield identical predictions regardless of when recommendations are requested. Equipment compatibility, duplication intent and replacement demand remain unobserved.
idea.implementation_notes:
Feasibility gate: verify that authorized training and inference interfaces supply aligned historical event timestamps, including repeated-item occurrences. The supplied (None, sequence, positive, negative) diagnostic batches and log2feats(sequence) alone do not establish this capability. Never recover event times through item-ID lookup, use target timestamps, or silently train with temporal inputs and predict without them. If the gate fails, defer this extension and retain the feasible uniform-negative HSTU control.

Preserve HSTU SiLU attention, gating, positional bias, normalization and the baseline objective for the initial temporal comparison. Explicitly depart from the official shifted-query convention: output row i predicts the next item but its temporal bias uses only abs(t_i - t_j) for historical keys j <= i. Do not copy a feature adapter that appends the target timestamp. Choose and record seconds as the common timestamp unit after checking source units. For valid pairs use bucket = clamp(floor(ln(max(abs(t_i-t_j),1))/0.301),0,128), with a separate missing-time bucket 129. Add a zero-initialized 130-entry temporal table per head. Preserve positional bias when timestamps are missing; this intentionally differs from reference behavior that can skip combined bias. Zero timestamps are missing only if the documented data format defines them as such. Padding is excluded independently of timestamp values.

Add finite temporal bias before SiLU; multiply the resulting weights by inclusive causal and query/key nonpadding masks afterward. Never substitute softmax-style negative infinity masking before SiLU. Maintain the corrected baseline’s attention scaling and normalization. Read out the greatest nonpadding index in LEFT-padded histories; define empty-history handling consistently with the baseline.

Extend log2feats through an optional aligned timestamp argument while retaining callable log2feats(sequence), item_emb and predict_score(features, items). The sequence-only call must have a documented missing-time behavior, but temporal diagnostics must use verified aligned times rather than report fallback results as temporal-model measurements. Keep view.model as the actual trained nn.Module. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). If batch timestamps cannot be obtained faithfully, report temporal probes unavailable with their reason. Preserve user_train, meta_data and review_data interfaces without inventing unavailable fields.

Update the predictor writer, checkpoint architecture configuration, bucket rule, timestamp units, masking and missing-time behavior together. The exported predictor must reproduce the same temporal preprocessing and scoring, loading exactly one checkpoint per category. No external encoder, pretrained weights or separately fitted popularity/transition scores are allowed.

Predeclare the actual configuration count, checkpoint evaluation frequency, stopping rule and GPU allocation before execution, within the remaining shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. The first temporal comparison is position-only versus position-plus-time with identical uniform-negative objectives, training budgets and checkpoint-selection opportunities. No-bias and time-only controls are secondary, budget permitting. Separately compare baseline, uniform multi-negative and lexical curriculum conditions using one fixed backbone; never fuse their outputs. Lexical sampling must exclude padding and known training positives, preserve uniform support and acknowledge unknown false negatives. State whether the loss is sampled candidate classification or a full-catalog approximation; any proposal correction requires explicit filtered proposal probabilities and separate handling of the always-included positive.

Use training-only temporal preprocessing. Check timestamp-origin invariance, equally spaced timestamps and shuffled consecutive gaps reconstructed into monotonic histories; the latter preserves gap distribution while breaking item alignment. Optional rate-normalized gaps require prefix-only medians, never future events, and a matched jointly trained rate-only control. Compare recent/old deletion with equal removal counts and retain the existing compaction/readout caveats. These probes remain in-sample; omitted paired-context effects provide no evidence of context sensitivity.

Preserve all four routes: Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl. Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, at most 200 epochs and 200 batches per epoch, one GPU, supplied splits and fixed host evaluation. Select using macro validation HR@10 with 200 users/category and 99 unique negative candidates, evaluation seed 42. Report category results and equal-weight macro results. Conditional paired user bootstrap intervals may describe fixed-candidate uncertainty, but do not capture training-seed variability or remove adaptive selection bias. Record failed attempts and compute cost; do not claim improvements before measurement, inspect hidden test data or change the evaluator.
idea.pseudocode:
Before training:
  verify aligned historical timestamps in authorized sampler and exported inference
  if unavailable:
    defer temporal extension; retain corrected HSTU uniform-negative control
  predeclare configurations, checkpoint schedule, stopping rule and budget
For each category independently, with training seed 42:
  initialize corrected HSTU
  add zero-initialized temporal_bias[head, 130]
  for each authorized batch within 200 epochs and 200 batches/epoch:
    obtain LEFT-padded items and occurrence-aligned historical timestamps
    valid = items != 0
    for historical pair (i,j):
      allowed = valid[i] and valid[j] and j <= i
      if either timestamp is genuinely unavailable:
        bucket[i,j] = 129
      else:
        gap_seconds = abs(t[i] - t[j])
        bucket[i,j] = clamp(floor(log(max(gap_seconds,1))/0.301),0,128)
    weights = SiLU(existing_similarity + position_bias + temporal_bias[bucket])
    weights = existing_scaling(weights) * allowed
    features = existing_HSTU_gated_aggregation(weights)
    optimize unchanged baseline next-item objective
  evaluate only at predeclared authorized validation checkpoints
  retain one selected checkpoint and its complete preprocessing configuration
  export the identical architecture through the predictor writer
At prediction:
  route to exactly one category checkpoint
  obtain only observed, occurrence-aligned history timestamps
  encode with identical temporal preprocessing and masking
  read features at the greatest nonpadding index
  score candidates using that network's predict_score
Diagnostics:
  retain all required interfaces and measured metric definitions
  verify independent timestamp-origin shifts leave predictions unchanged
  measure reconstructed shuffled-gap and matched context-removal effects
  label unavailable timestamp probes and in-sample limitations explicitly

originality.positive: The proposal adapts temporal HSTU to the supplied LEFT-padded, historical-input-only setting and explicitly removes dependence on unavailable target-time context.
originality.negative: Relative temporal bias is established in HSTU; leakage-free interface adaptation is necessary engineering rather than a new modeling principle.

future_potential.positive: A compact temporal mechanism can test whether within-history spacing improves current-task relevance while retaining useful older interests.
future_potential.negative: Timestamp plumbing is unverified, post-history inactivity is unidentifiable, and neither the diagnostics nor cited experiments establish gains on the pinned datasets.

code_difficulty.positive: The added parameters are small, jointly trained and compatible with a single HSTU checkpoint.
code_difficulty.negative: Occurrence-level timestamp alignment, causal query semantics, LEFT-padding masks, diagnostic adaptation and consistent predictor export create substantial integration risk.

related_work.title: Actions Speak Louder than Words: Trillion-Parameter Sequential Transducers for Generative Recommendations
contributions: Introduces HSTU with gated aggregation and relative positional and temporal bias added before SiLU.
Provides direct architectural precedent for the selected extension.
limitations: Does not establish improvements on the four pinned Amazon tasks.
Temporal bias neither imposes monotonic decay nor identifies purchase intent.
Reference timestamp alignment must be adapted explicitly to this task’s prohibition on target-time inputs.

related_work.title: Official HSTU research implementation
contributions: Makes temporal bucketing, shifted query timestamps and post-SiLU causal masking explicit.
Provides implementation details needed to distinguish the proposed historical-query adaptation from the reference.
limitations: Its sequence layout and timestamp semantics cannot be copied directly into this LEFT-padded host.
Individual missing timestamps lack the explicit missing bucket proposed here.

related_work.title: Official HSTU sequential feature adapter
contributions: Shows how target timestamps can be placed after history for reference offline evaluation.
limitations: That target-time context is unavailable and prohibited for this experiment.
The host’s aligned historical timestamp and request-time interfaces remain unverified.

related_work.title: Scaling New Frontiers: HSTU component ablations
contributions: Provides precedent for comparing positional, temporal and combined attention-bias components.
limitations: Reported findings do not determine outcomes under this host’s inputs, sampled candidates or compute budget.

related_work.title: Long-Term Interest Clock
contributions: Motivates using time gaps to recover relevant long-term behaviors.
limitations: Does not establish gains for this constrained HSTU experiment.
Historical gaps alone cannot identify elapsed inactivity after the final observed event.

related_work.title: Study of recency bias in recommendation
contributions: Provides evidence that excessive recency bias can harm recommendation accuracy.
limitations: Does not determine suitable temporal weighting for the four datasets.

related_work.title: Sequential recommendation negative-sampling study
contributions: Compares sampling strategies and identifies dataset-dependent accuracy and popularity tradeoffs.
limitations: Does not establish that lexical negatives improve the pinned benchmark.
Unobserved items can be valid alternatives rather than true negatives.

related_work.title: Correcting the LogQ Correction
contributions: Highlights the different inclusion mechanisms of always-present positives and sampled negatives.
limitations: Does not justify an unspecified correction for filtered lexical sampling.
A practical experiment still requires an explicit objective and proposal distribution.

related_work.title: HSTU-BLaIR
contributions: Provides precedent for augmenting HSTU item representations with textual information.
limitations: Its pretrained text encoder is unavailable under the task constraints.
Reported gains do not establish effectiveness of a title/description encoder trained from scratch.
Text similarity does not certify product compatibility.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains how repeated model selection can overfit a finite validation criterion.
limitations: Predeclared trials and checkpoint opportunities limit adaptivity but do not make selected validation scores unbiased.
The host’s untouched final evaluation remains necessary.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled recommendation metrics can disagree with full-catalog model rankings.
limitations: Does not authorize changing the pinned evaluator.
Fixed-candidate confidence intervals do not establish full-catalog quality.
